lesson_1.watch_out: Julius Caesar raided Britain in 55 and 54 BC, yet he sailed away without conquering the island—full Roman conquest waited nearly a century until AD 43.

passage.bullet: Master smiths twisted pure gold torcs and beat bronze shields → proved advanced artistic skill

lesson_1.watch_out: Never assume Iron Age Britons were backward just because they left no written books—gold torcs, bronze shields, and stater coins prove high skill.

passage.bullet: Roman senators doubted Claudius over his limp and stutter → he needed military glory in AD 43

lesson_2.watch_out: Claudius did not invade Britain for one single reason—he combined his personal need to impress Roman senators with greed for metals, wheat, and taxes.

passage.bullet: Flexible lorica segmentata iron strips and locked testudo shields → protected marching legionaries from arrows

lesson_2.watch_out: Roman legionaries did not win by swinging giant heavy swords wildly—they stayed calm behind locked shields and stabbed neatly with a short gladius.

passage.bullet: General Aulus Plautius landed at Richborough with four legions → defeated Caratacus at the River Medway

lesson_2.watch_out: Emperor Claudius did not fight the whole invasion himself—General Aulus Plautius won the tough River Medway battle first and waited for Claudius to claim glory.

passage.bullet: Dying ally King Prasutagus shared wealth with Emperor Nero → greedy Roman officials broke that promise

lesson_3.watch_out: The Iceni had not fought Rome from the very start—King Prasutagus was a peaceful Roman ally until officials betrayed his will in AD 60.

passage.bullet: Governor Suetonius Paulinus was away fighting in Anglesey → left southern Roman towns poorly defended

lesson_3.watch_out: Boudicca did not burn just one city—her rebel alliance destroyed three separate Roman settlements: Camulodunum, Londinium, and Verulamium.

passage.bullet: Paulinus positioned 10,000 legionaries inside a narrow wooded valley → funnelled and squashed charging Britons

stems.stem: Outnumbered in AD 61, Paulinus chose a ____________ so the huge rebel army could not surround his ____________ legionaries.

lesson_3.watch_out: Having a much bigger army did not guarantee victory—narrow valley ground and parked family wagons turned British numbers into a deadly trap.

passage.bullet: Hadrian ordered a 73-mile stone wall from Wallsend to Bowness-on-Solway → divided Roman Britain from Caledonia

lesson_4.watch_out: Hadrian's Wall does not follow the modern England–Scotland border, and its milecastle gates controlled trade and taxes rather than sealing everyone out.

passage.bullet: Wet, oxygen-free mud stopped wood rotting → preserved hundreds of thin ink tablets from AD 100
